findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the endpoint's datetime ordering key
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies the numeric Paginator implementation and calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. value_from_cursor also returns the raw millisecond cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does, so build_queryset compares the datetime column against a number. Any optimized request that returns rows (or builds next/prev cursors via build_cursor) will 500 instead of paginating.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed directly into queryset slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set, a user-supplied cursor offset < 0 is used verbatim as queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor strings are attacker-controlled (Cursor.from_string accepts any integer), so an authorized admin/superuser can craft offsets such as -1000000. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), causing unhandled 500s, and if this pattern is reused with list-backed querysets it wraps around and returns rows outside the intended page bounds. Other paginators in this file validate this case and raise BadPaginationError; this path adds no validation, bound, or max_offset check.

findings.title: BasePaginator change exposes all existing paginated endpoints to negative-offset crashes
findings.body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result now branches on is_prev: for prev cursors the raw cursor.offset is still passed to queryset[offset:stop], and the comment claims 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions'. It does not: Django raises AssertionError on negative slices. Because this edits the base class used by every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint, any user who can supply a crafted prev cursor with a negative offset to any existing endpoint can trigger an unhandled 500. The change also silently changes non-prev behavior (clamping to 0) without tests for either direction.

findings.title: Unconditional member access can crash requests for users without a member record
findings.body: enable_advanced is computed on every GET, even when optimized_pagination is not requested: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. For a non-superuser whose organization_context.member is None (e.g. access granted without a member row), this raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working default DateTimePaginator path for all audit-log requests, not just optimized ones. The check should be short-circuited behind use_optimized and guard against member being None.

findings.title: Cursor offset remains unvalidated while PR relies on negative offsets being safe
findings.body: Cursor.__init__ stores int(offset) with no lower bound, and from_string therefore accepts arbitrary negative offsets from the query string. The added comment asserts this 'enables efficient reverse pagination', but no consumer validates it: SequencePaginator asserts offset > -1, OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets, and Django querysets raise AssertionError. Landing the comment/behavior contract without central validation leaves each paginator to fail inconsistently (assert, 500, or wrap-around) on the same crafted cursor.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, changes BasePaginator slicing, and adds an optimized branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but includes no tests. There is no coverage that optimized pagination returns correct next/prev cursors for datetime keys, that negative offsets are rejected rather than crashing or leaking out-of-page rows, or that non-admin/non-optimized requests still work. Given the datetime-key and negative-slice failures above, tests exercising a real multi-page audit-log request with optimized_pagination=true would have caught the breakage before merge.
